Execution of US murderer Christa Pike halted shortly before it was due to happen
- Published
The execution of Tennessee inmate Christa Pike has been halted just over an hour before it was due to happen.
Pike, 50, has been awaiting execution since she was convicted and sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.
In their ruling on Wednesday, judges from the Sixth Circuit Appeals court said they needed more time to consider the arguments in Pike's case.

facts_zh:
Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations
- Published
Animal rights activists have criticised Botswana's decision to authorise the killing of 23 elephants to provide meat for independence celebrations.
The southern African country, home to the world's largest elephant population, is holding nationwide festivities on Wednesday to mark the 60th anniversary of independence from Britain.
A licence issued by the Ministry of Environment and Tourism, seen by local media, authorises the hunting of 23 elephants and other wild animals for "complimentary purposes".

articles.title_zh: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
facts_zh:
Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
- Published
The last British and American troops have left Iraq after a military presence of more than a decade in the country.
The exit of the remaining UK military personnel - around 100 - from Irbil, in the northern Kurdistan region, was co-ordinated over recent weeks with US forces, who also departed on Wednesday.
It follows an agreement between the US and the Iraqi government, signed two years ago, to withdraw foreign troops by the end of this month.

Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests
- Published
Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote and Kenya's President William Ruto have broken ground on a $16bn (£12bn) oil refinery in Lamu, on Kenya's northern coast.
Upon completion, the refinery is expected to process 700,000 barrels of crude oil a day, making it East Africa's largest industrial project by capacity.
Ahead of the launch, some local residents took to the streets to demand more compensation for land used for the refinery.

articles.title_zh: South Korea demands apology from Pyongyang for landmine blasts that injured three
facts_zh:
South Korea demands apology from Pyongyang for landmine blasts that injured three
- Published
South Korea's military has demanded an apology from North Korea for landmine blasts along their shared border that wounded South Korean soldiers earlier this month.
Three South Korean personnel were injured by explosions in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) - a buffer zone separating the two Koreas, on 21 September.
South Korea said on Tuesday it was "certain" that the blasts, which happened on South Korea's side of the DMZ, came from North Korean mines.

articles.title_original: Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
facts_zh:
Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
Six-year-old Raseel al-Balawi in Gaza has had more than 20 surgeries since an Israeli air strike injured her in late July.
Witnesses say her tent in al-Mawasi camp was hit by a strike from an Israeli helicopter, and she now has to have frequent surgeries to try and control infections in her wounds.
Israel's military says it has no record of the attack and that it "regrets any harm to civilians".

all_titles.en: Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
